GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2018-09-21T02:24:17Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Access timestamps from createdAt/updatedAt instead of custom field name
Description: In current sequelize, when a custom column name has been assigned to one of the timestamps, the timestamp value is no longer accessible from Model.createdAt / updated.At etc.

From my understanding, this [v5 change](/sequelize/sequelize/issues/6423#issuecomment-379472035) will only change the behavior when timestamps are not customized.

I'm a very new user of sequelize, but tbh I think this is inconsistent, isn't it? What is the reason behind this design? (Please consider this as a feature request)

## What are you doing?
```js
const MyTable = sequelize.define('mytable', {
  myField: {
    type: Sequelize.INTEGER,
    field: 'my_column',
  },
}, {
  createdAt: 'my_created_at',
  updatedAt: false,
});
MyTable.create({
  myField: 0,
})).then(myInstance => {
  console.log(myInstance.myField); // 0
  console.log(myInstance.createdAt); // undefined
  console.log(myInstance.my_created_at); // createdAt timestamp
});
```

## What do you expect to happen?
myInstance.createdAt shows the createdAt timestamp.

__Dialect:__ mysql
__Sequelize version:__ 4.38.1
